issues.description: Test changes pass a zero-amount addition that contradicts CreateSignedTransaction's __post_init__ intent
issues.detail: The tests now pass `additions=[Addition(amount=uint64(0), puzzle_hash=bytes32.zeros)]` to cat_spend. The invariant `len(self.additions) < 1` check in CreateSignedTransaction is bypassed by a sentinel zero-amount, zero-puzzle addition. Either the invariant is wrong (should allow empty additions when CAT discrepancy is in play) or the test is smuggling a placeholder. State which.

issues.description: cat_discrepancy_validation uses `None in {a, b, c}` which is correct but unreadable and fragile
issues.detail: The set-membership check works but obscures the invariant: "either all three are None or none are." A literate version would write `any(x is None for x in (extra_delta, tail_reveal, tail_solution))` after the all-None early return, and the type-ignore comments would not be necessary if a local narrowing assertion stated the invariant explicitly.

issues.description: Silent loss of memos field semantics when additions are forwarded through CreateSignedTransaction
issues.detail: Old send_transaction passed `memos=[[mem.encode("utf-8") for mem in request.memos]]` (bytes-encoded). The new path wraps `request.memos` (list[str]) into an `Addition.memos: list[str] | None`. The downstream encoding contract must be audited: are these still encoded to bytes before signing, or has the encoding boundary silently shifted? State the invariant and verify.

issues.description: CreateSignedTransaction now carries CAT-specific fields with no validation of mutual exclusivity
issues.detail: extra_delta/tail_reveal/tail_solution and puzzle_decorator are now first-class fields on a general-purpose endpoint. There is no __post_init__ check that, e.g., CAT discrepancy fields are only valid for CAT wallets. The type now admits nonsensical states (XCH send with tail_reveal set). Add an invariant or accept the documentation debt explicitly.

issues.description: `get_wallet(...)` called only "for opportunity to raise" — discarded return value is a code smell
issues.detail: The comment `# opportunity to raise` acknowledges the call exists solely for its side effect of validation. This is the kind of code a reader stumbles over. Extract a `_validate_wallet_type(wallet_id, required_type)` method whose name states the intent, or document the invariant that create_signed_transaction does not re-check wallet type.

issues.description: Two structurally identical cat_discrepancy properties duplicate the delegation pattern
issues.detail: Both CATSpend.cat_discrepancy and CreateSignedTransaction.cat_discrepancy are one-line forwarders to cat_discrepancy_validation. A mixin or a shared protocol would make the relationship explicit; as written, a future field rename will require updating both call sites silently. Minor, but worth a literate comment noting the shared contract.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED. The refactor's intent — collapse three near-duplicate endpoints into one — is sound and the extracted `cat_discrepancy_validation` is a legitimate deduplication. But several invariants are now implicit where they used to be explicit: the test patches around a length-1-minimum additions invariant with a zero-sentinel addition, CAT-specific fields now live on a general transaction type with no mutual-exclusivity check, and the memos encoding boundary appears to shift without comment. NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT on the new combined type to state which field combinations are valid, and the `# opportunity to raise` comment should become a named method. The algorithm is fine; the contract documentation is missing.
